old.title: Reimagine business productivity with AI agents and assistants
old.summary: IBM AI Academy instructor Parul Mishra explains the difference between a human-directed AI assistant and an agent capable of carrying out workflows. The 7:58 lesson examines how both can improve employee productivity and how teams should decide which type of assistance fits a business task. This is an evergreen March 2025 instructional overview.
old.why_it_matters: Knowledge workers can avoid confusing fluent chat with delegated autonomy by mapping a real workflow and identifying which steps need assistance, which merit permitted automation and where human review remains essential.

new.title: Putting AI to work for integration
new.summary: IBM AI Academy instructor Madhu Kochar explains how enterprises link applications, data and business tasks so AI-assisted work can move across systems without losing oversight. The 5:31 educational lesson covers practical integration value, governance guardrails and where AI agents fit into reliable workflows. This November 2025 episode is evergreen instruction, not new product news.
new.why_it_matters: Before delegating an office workflow to an AI agent, map the systems exchanging information, the permissions required and where people must approve changes. Choose one bounded integration and test its outcomes rather than assuming an agent can safely operate across every system.
new.learning_objective: Evaluate how integration architecture, governance controls and agent autonomy affect trustworthy cross-system work.
new.practical_action: Map one cross-app handoff, identify permissions and approvals, define a fallback when integration fails, and verify the workflow with real examples.
transferrable_takeaways: Reliable agent workflows require trustworthy connections among existing applications, data and business systems.
Governance and guardrails should be designed into each cross-system tool boundary before agents take actions.
A small, measurable integration with human approval offers a safer pilot than broad unattended automation.
